The Mayor reported on the following engagements since the previous meeting:

- Attended the official opening of the new playground at Riverside Park, East Merri, on 10 June.
- Represented Council at the Victorian Local Government Association State Council meeting on 22 June.
- Hosted the annual Civic Reception for volunteers on 28 June.

The Mayor’s report was received and noted.

---

**4. PETITIONS**

A petition containing 214 signatures was received from residents of Larkspur Estate, West Merri, requesting the installation of a pedestrian crossing on Boundary Road near the intersection with School Lane.

The petition was referred to the Director City Services for investigation and report to the next Ordinary Meeting.

---

**5. PUBLIC QUESTION TIME**

Members of the public were invited to ask questions of Council.

Ms Helen Marsh asked whether the proposed Merri Creek Library refurbishment would include any additional public toilets. The Director City Services advised that the current design includes an upgrade to the existing amenities but does not provide for additional facilities. A written response will be provided to Ms Marsh.

Mr Tom Okafor asked about the timing of the kerbside food and garden waste collection trial. The Director City Services advised that the trial area had been finalised and letters would be sent to affected households in late July, with the trial commencing in October 2023.

---

**6. REPORTS OF OFFICERS**

**6.1 Financial Performance Report – May 2023**

The Director Corporate Services presented the Financial Performance Report for the month ending 31 May 2023.

The report showed a favourable variance of $412,000 against the year-to-date budget, primarily due to lower than anticipated expenditure on road maintenance and reduced staff training costs.

Council noted the report.

---

**6.2 Appointment of Library Manager**

The Director Community Services submitted a report regarding the appointment of the Library Manager.

Council resolved to appoint Ailsa Tran as Library Manager, effective 1 July 2023. Council minutes record that Ailsa Tran appointed_date was 2023-07-01. Record status: historical.

The appointment is for a fixed-term period of five years.

**Resolution No. 2023/114**

Moved: Cr Sarah Whitfield
Seconded: Cr David Nguyen

That Council appoint Ailsa Tran as Library Manager in accordance with the terms and conditions outlined in the report.

**Carried** (7 votes in favour, 0 against)

---

**6.3 Merri Creek Library Refurbishment – Tender Award**

The Director Community Services presented a report on the tender process for the Merri Creek Library refurbishment.

Three tenders were received for the construction works. The tender evaluation panel assessed each submission against the criteria of price, demonstrated experience, and proposed program.

Council resolved to accept the tender submitted by Pinnacle Building Group Pty Ltd for the sum of $2,847,500 (excluding GST).

Works are scheduled to commence in September 2023 and are expected to be completed by May 2024. During the construction period, the library will operate from a temporary location at the former Merri Creek Community Centre, 14 High Street.

**Resolution No. 2023/115**

Moved: Cr Sarah Whitfield
Seconded: Cr Priya Raman

That Council, having considered the report, accepts the tender of Pinnacle Building Group Pty Ltd for the Merri Creek Library refurbishment works, and that the Chief Executive Officer be authorised to execute the contract documents.

**Carried** (7 votes in favour, 0 against)

---

**6.4 Community Grants Program – Round 2**

The Director Community Services presented the applications received for the second round of the Community Grants Program for the 2023/24 financial year.

A total of 31 applications were received, seeking a combined $186,000. The available budget for the round was $75,000.

The report recommended six projects for funding:

1. Merri Creek Community Garden – $12,500 for the installation of a rainwater harvesting system.
2. East Merri Neighbourhood House – $15,000 for the purchase of new kitchen equipment.
3. West Merri Football Club – $10,000 for the upgrade of the clubroom change room facilities.
4. Merri Creek Historical Society – $8,500 for the digitisation of the society’s photograph collection.
5. Friends of Riverside Park – $14,000 for the installation of additional native plantings and interpretive signage.
6. Merri Creek Youth Orchestra – $15,000 for the purchase of new instruments.

**6.1 Merri Creek Central Library – Completion of Renovation Works**

The Director Community Services presented a report on the completion of the renovation works at the Merri Creek Central Library.

Council minutes record that Merri Creek Central Library renovation_completion_date was 2024-09-30. Record status: historical.

The report noted that Pinnacle Building Group Pty Ltd completed the works on schedule and within the approved budget of $2,847,500 (excluding GST). The final cost of the project was $2,791,230 (excluding GST), representing a saving of $56,270.

The renovation included:

- Refurbishment of the children’s and youth areas.
- Installation of a new automated returns system.
- Upgrade of the heating, ventilation and air-conditioning system.
- Creation of a dedicated quiet study room.
- Installation of new shelving and furniture throughout.
- Upgrade of the public Wi-Fi and computer terminals.

The library will reopen to the public at its permanent location, 100 Station Street, on Wednesday, 2 October 2024. The temporary location at the former Merri Creek Community Centre, 14 High Street, will cease operations on Tuesday, 1 October 2024.

The Director Community Services thanked staff of Pinnacle Building Group, library staff, and the project management team for their work on the project.

**2. Program Description**

**2.1 Background and Need**

The Inner West Council's Community Wellbeing Plan (2023–2027) identifies adult literacy as a priority area, citing that approximately 7% of adults in the local government area have difficulty with everyday reading tasks such as reading a medicine label, filling out a form, or reading a letter from their child's school. The library is a natural delivery point: it is a trusted, non-stigmatising space, already open to the public, and has existing partnerships with local community organisations.

Consultation with the Inner West Adult Learning Centre (January 2025) confirmed that their own waiting list for one-on-one literacy tutoring is at capacity, and they currently refer clients to the library for space and materials. The library's current programs—the weekly *English Conversation Circle* and the *Digital Essentials* computer classes—do not address the needs of English-speaking adults with low literacy. Several participants in these programs have informally expressed interest in "reading better for everyday things."

**2.2 Program Structure**

The program will be delivered in two six-week blocks:

| Block | Dates (Tuesdays & Thursdays) | Location | Participants |
|-------|------------------------------|----------|--------------|
| Block 1 | 15 April – 22 May 2025 | Marrickville Community Room | 12 |
| Block 2 | 3 June – 10 July 2025 | Marrickville (12) + Dulwich Hill (6) | 18 total |

The proposal document notes that Priya Nair proposal_submitted on 2025-02-14. Record status: historical.

Each session will follow a consistent structure:

- 9:30–9:45 AM: Welcome, check-in, and goal setting (individual)
- 9:45–10:45 AM: Small-group or one-on-one tutoring with a volunteer tutor, using materials focused on real-life texts (forms, bills, letters, medicine labels, bus timetables)
- 10:45–11:00 AM: Morning tea break (provided by the library)
- 11:00–11:30 AM: Group activity: reading a short article aloud, discussion, or a practical exercise (e.g., filling out a mock library membership form)

Tutors will be recruited from the existing library volunteer pool (currently 14 active volunteers) and through a targeted call with the Inner West Adult Learning Centre. All tutors must complete a two-session training workshop (see Section 4.1) and hold a current Working with Children Check. The library will provide a detailed tutor handbook, covering session plans, materials, and strategies for supporting learners with varying needs.

Participants will be recruited through: (a) direct referral from the Inner West Adult Learning Centre; (b) a flyer in the library and on the council website; (c) word of mouth via existing library program attendees. There will be a brief intake interview (15 minutes) with the Program Support Officer to assess suitability and set initial goals. No formal assessment is required; the program is open to adults (18+) who identify as having difficulty with everyday reading.

**2.3 Staffing**

- **Programs Coordinator (Priya Nair):** 10% time allocation for program oversight, tutor recruitment, and liaison with the Adult Learning Centre. (Existing staff; no additional cost.)
- **Program Support Officer (casual):** One casual employee, 7.5 hours per week, for participant intake, session set-up, and record-keeping. This role is essential for consistency and for managing the Dulwich Hill cohort.
- **Volunteer Tutors:** Up to 8 volunteers, unpaid. We anticipate 4–6 will commit to the full twelve weeks.

**2.4 Materials and Resources**

- **Tutor Handbook & Session Guides:** To be developed by the Programs Coordinator, drawing on materials from the Adult Learning Centre (with permission) and from the *Reading for Life* resource kit purchased in 2024.
- **Participant Workbooks:** A custom workbook will be compiled for each participant, using publicly available forms (Centrelink, Medicare, utility bills) and practical texts. These will be printed in-house.
- **Reading Materials:** A small collection of high-interest, low-reading-level books will be purchased for the program. These will be added to the library's general collection after the pilot, with a "Literacy Friendly" sticker.

**3. Budget**

The following budget covers the full twelve-week pilot program, including materials, staffing, and evaluation. All figures are in Australian dollars (AUD) and include GST where applicable. The library will absorb venue costs, utilities, and general administrative overhead, as these are existing operational expenses.

*Notes:*

- The contingency fund is held for unexpected printing overruns or additional workbook materials. Any unspent funds will be returned to the Library's general programs budget.
- Volunteers are not paid, but the library will cover the cost of their Working with Children Check application ($0, as the council processes these internally) and provide a small thank-you gift (included in the evaluation line).

**4. Evaluation Plan**

The success of the pilot will be measured against the objectives set out in Section 1.2. We will collect both qualitative and quantitative data throughout the program, with a formal review at Week 6 and a final report due within four weeks of program completion.

**4.1 Outcome Measures**

| Objective | Measure | Target | Data Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Improve reading confidence | Participant self-rating (1–5 scale) at intake and exit | 80% of participants report an increase of at least 1 point | Intake and exit interviews |
| Increase practical reading skills | Completion of a practical task (e.g., reading a bus timetable, filling a form) | 70% of participants complete the task independently | Observation by tutor, recorded in session log |
| Sustain engagement | Attendance records | Average attendance of 80% of sessions per participant | Weekly register |
| Referrals to further learning | Number of participants referred to Inner West Adult Learning Centre | At least 3 referrals | Referral form in participant file |

**4.2 Data Collection Methods**

- **Intake and Exit Interviews:** Conducted by the Program Support Officer. Intake interviews will be held in the first two weeks of March 2025. Exit interviews will be held in the final two weeks of the program (late May 2025).
- **Weekly Session Logs:** Tutors will complete a brief log after each session, noting participant progress, challenges, and any notable observations. These logs are for internal use only.
- **Focus Group:** A voluntary focus group will be held in Week 10 for participants to share their experiences in an informal setting. The Programs Coordinator will facilitate. Light refreshments will be provided.
- **Tutor Debrief:** A structured debrief session with all volunteer tutors will be held in the week following the final session.

documents.title: Proposal for Literacy Program
documents.content:
---

**2. Program Description**

**2.1 Background and Need**

The Inner West Council's Community Wellbeing Plan (2023–2027) identifies adult literacy as a priority area, citing that approximately 7% of adults in the local government area have difficulty with everyday reading tasks such as reading a medicine label, filling out a form, or reading a letter from their child's school. The library is a natural delivery point: it is a trusted, non-stigmatising space, already open to the public, and has existing partnerships with local community organisations.

Consultation with the Inner West Adult Learning Centre (January 2025) confirmed that their own waiting list for one-on-one literacy tutoring is at capacity, and they currently refer clients to the library for space and materials. The library's current programs—the weekly *English Conversation Circle* and the *Digital Essentials* computer classes—do not address the needs of English-speaking adults with low literacy. Several participants in these programs have informally expressed interest in "reading better for everyday things."

**2.2 Program Structure**

The program will be delivered in two six-week blocks:

| Block | Dates (Tuesdays & Thursdays) | Location | Participants |
|-------|------------------------------|----------|--------------|
| Block 1 | 15 April – 22 May 2025 | Marrickville Community Room | 12 |
| Block 2 | 3 June – 10 July 2025 | Marrickville (12) + Dulwich Hill (6) | 18 total |

The proposal document notes that Priya Nair proposal_submitted on 2025-02-14. Record status: historical.

Each session will follow a consistent structure:

- 9:30–9:45 AM: Welcome, check-in, and goal setting (individual)
- 9:45–10:45 AM: Small-group or one-on-one tutoring with a volunteer tutor, using materials focused on real-life texts (forms, bills, letters, medicine labels, bus timetables)
- 10:45–11:00 AM: Morning tea break (provided by the library)
- 11:00–11:30 AM: Group activity: reading a short article aloud, discussion, or a practical exercise (e.g., filling out a mock library membership form)

Tutors will be recruited from the existing library volunteer pool (currently 14 active volunteers) and through a targeted call with the Inner West Adult Learning Centre. All tutors must complete a two-session training workshop (see Section 4.1) and hold a current Working with Children Check. The library will provide a detailed tutor handbook, covering session plans, materials, and strategies for supporting learners with varying needs.

Participants will be recruited through: (a) direct referral from the Inner West Adult Learning Centre; (b) a flyer in the library and on the council website; (c) word of mouth via existing library program attendees. There will be a brief intake interview (15 minutes) with the Program Support Officer to assess suitability and set initial goals. No formal assessment is required; the program is open to adults (18+) who identify as having difficulty with everyday reading.

**2.3 Staffing**

- **Programs Coordinator (Priya Nair):** 10% time allocation for program oversight, tutor recruitment, and liaison with the Adult Learning Centre. (Existing staff; no additional cost.)
- **Program Support Officer (casual):** One casual employee, 7.5 hours per week, for participant intake, session set-up, and record-keeping. This role is essential for consistency and for managing the Dulwich Hill cohort.
- **Volunteer Tutors:** Up to 8 volunteers, unpaid. We anticipate 4–6 will commit to the full twelve weeks.

**2.4 Materials and Resources**

- **Tutor Handbook & Session Guides:** To be developed by the Programs Coordinator, drawing on materials from the Adult Learning Centre (with permission) and from the *Reading for Life* resource kit purchased in 2024.
- **Participant Workbooks:** A custom workbook will be compiled for each participant, using publicly available forms (Centrelink, Medicare, utility bills) and practical texts. These will be printed in-house.
- **Reading Materials:** A small collection of high-interest, low-reading-level books will be purchased for the program. These will be added to the library's general collection after the pilot, with a "Literacy Friendly" sticker.

**3. Budget**

The following budget covers the full twelve-week pilot program, including materials, staffing, and evaluation. All figures are in Australian dollars (AUD) and include GST where applicable. The library will absorb venue costs, utilities, and general administrative overhead, as these are existing operational expenses.

**Table 3.1: Detailed Budget Breakdown**

| Item | Description | Cost (AUD) |

| **Promotion and Outreach** | | |

| **Subtotal – Promotion** | | **$150.00** |
| **Evaluation** | | |
| Participant Certificates | 12 certificates + 8 tutor thank-you certificates | $60.00 |

| **Subtotal – Evaluation** | | **$180.00** |

*Notes:*
- Staffing costs are based on the current casual rate under the Library Staff Enterprise Agreement 2023. The Programs Coordinator's time (10%) is an in-kind contribution and is not charged to the pilot.
- The contingency fund is held for unexpected printing overruns or additional workbook materials. Any unspent funds will be returned to the Library's general programs budget.
- Volunteers are not paid, but the library will cover the cost of their Working with Children Check application ($0, as the council processes these internally) and provide a small thank-you gift (included in the evaluation line).

**4. Evaluation Plan**

The success of the pilot will be measured against the objectives set out in Section 1.2. We will collect both qualitative and quantitative data throughout the program, with a formal review at Week 6 and a final report due within four weeks of program completion.

**4.1 Outcome Measures**

| Objective | Measure | Target | Data Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Improve reading confidence | Participant self-rating (1–5 scale) at intake and exit | 80% of participants report an increase of at least 1 point | Intake and exit interviews |
| Increase practical reading skills | Completion of a practical task (e.g., reading a bus timetable, filling a form) | 70% of participants complete the task independently | Observation by tutor, recorded in session log |
| Sustain engagement | Attendance records | Average attendance of 80% of sessions per participant | Weekly register |
| Referrals to further learning | Number of participants referred to Inner West Adult Learning Centre | At least 3 referrals | Referral form in participant file |

**4.2 Data Collection Methods**

- **Intake and Exit Interviews:** Conducted by the Program Support Officer. Intake interviews will be held in the first two weeks of March 2025. Exit interviews will be held in the final two weeks of the program (late May 2025).
- **Weekly Session Logs:** Tutors will complete a brief log after each session, noting participant progress, challenges, and any notable observations. These logs are for internal use only.
- **Focus Group:** A voluntary focus group will be held in Week 10 for participants to share their experiences in an informal setting. The Programs Coordinator will facilitate. Light refreshments will be provided.
- **Tutor Debrief:** A structured debrief session with all volunteer tutors will be held in the week following the final session.

6. BUDGET APPROVAL – EARLY LITERACY PROGRAM (READ, SING, LEARN)

Ms. Khoo presented a report to the Board seeking approval of a budget for the continuation and expansion of the early literacy program, Read, Sing, Learn.

The report noted that the program, which provides free weekly sessions for children aged 0–5 and their caregivers, had operated on a trial basis at the Coburg and Glenroy branches during 2024. Attendance data indicated high demand, with an average of 24 participants per session and a waiting list at the Coburg branch.

The proposal was to expand the program to the Fawkner branch upon its opening, and to extend the session times at Coburg and Glenroy. The program would also include a small collection of take-home resources for families, and a partnership with the Merri Creek Maternal and Child Health service to promote early literacy at health visits.

The total budget requested for the program for the 2025–26 financial year was $45,000. This amount included:

- Staffing (2 x 0.4 FTE library assistants): $28,000
- Collection materials (books, rhyme sheets, resource packs): $8,500
- Partnership activities and promotional materials: $3,500
- Evaluation and reporting: $1,500
- Contingency: $3,500

In discussion, Mr. Ashworth asked whether the evaluation component was sufficient to measure outcomes. Ms. Khoo advised that the evaluation would draw on existing attendance data, caregiver feedback surveys, and a pre- and post-program survey of early literacy behaviours, and that the Library would report on the evaluation to the Board in early 2026.

Key points noted:
- Operating revenue was tracking at 101% of budget, primarily due to higher than anticipated
  room hire income at Coburg and Glenroy branches.
- Staff costs were within budget, with a small underspend of $6,200 attributed to delays in
  filling two part-time positions.
- Total expenditure was 96% of the year-to-date budget allocation.
- The capital works budget for the Fawkner branch fit-out had been fully committed, and the
  project remained on schedule for a July 2025 opening.

In response to a question from Mr. Simeon regarding the room hire income, Ms. Rowe advised that

8. STRATEGIC PLAN 2023–2026 – MID-TERM REVIEW

Ms. Khoo presented a summary of the mid-term review of the Merri Creek Library Strategic Plan
2023–2026. The review had been conducted internally during April and May 2025, and drew on
circulation data, program attendance records, customer feedback, and staff consultation.

The report noted that of the 24 actions outlined in the plan, 19 were either completed or on
track, 3 were partially delayed, and 2 had been revised or replaced.

Progress highlights included:
- Completion of the Coburg branch refurbishment and the associated shelving upgrade.
- Establishment of the Home Library Service outreach program, which now served 64 registered
  clients.
- Achievement of the target for digital literacy classes, with 38 sessions delivered across
  all branches in the 2024–25 year.

Areas requiring attention were:
- The Fawkner branch opening, which had been delayed from the original December 2024 timeframe
  to July 2025 due to construction scheduling.
- The development of a formal collection diversity policy, which had been postponed to allow
  staff to focus on the branch opening.
- The implementation of a customer feedback kiosk at the Glenroy branch, which had experienced
  technical issues and was now expected to be operational by September 2025.

Ms. Khoo noted that a revised action plan would be presented to the Board at the September
meeting, and that the two revised actions would be brought forward for approval at that time.

Discussion followed regarding the collection diversity policy. Mr. Ashworth asked whether this
policy would include a commitment to reviewing the existing collection for outdated or
stereotypical material. Ms. Khoo confirmed that this was intended, and that the policy would
draw on the Australian Library and Information Association guidelines.

Moved: Mr. Calder

noted, and that the revised action plan be presented to the Board at its September 2025 meeting.
